body: # Day 09 Exercise Refatortor Api.js for tickets assignments for the last 3 days ago --- ## Describe This project is an advanced iteration of the previous Ticket Management system. The architecture has been upgraded to meet industry standards for scalability, security, and observability. ## New Features & Enhancements ### 1. Clean Architecture Refactoring The entire project has been refactored using **Clean Architecture** principles. By separating the code into distinct layers (Entities, Use Cases, Repositories, and Interfaces), the business logic is now decoupled from external frameworks, making the system more maintainable and testable. ### 2. JSON Data Persistence The system now utilizes **JSON files** to store dummy data. This replaces in-memory storage, ensuring that ticket and user information is persistent and can be managed dynamically. ### 3. Security Layer (Authentication) A robust security layer has been implemented to protect sensitive data: * **Authentication**: Users are now required to log in to the system before they can retrieve or view data. * **User Database**: A dedicated user database has been integrated to manage credentials and roles. * **Admin Privileges**: A restricted endpoint `../assign` has been added, which is accessible exclusively by users with **Admin** status. ### 4. Advanced Logging with Winston The logging system has been upgraded by replacing *Morgan* with **Winston**. This change allows for: * Structured logging with different priority levels (Info, Warn, Error). * Persistent log storage by saving output to local files instead of just the console. --- *Completed by Theodore Raphaello* for proof of successful program execution screenshot - GET /tickets -POST /auth/register -POST /auth/login -GET / tickets || using barier token -PATCH / tickets/id: -LOGGING with winston

body:
### Motivation
- When a student completes a test the system should use the `Attempt.result` and the student's `schedulesPref` to find an appropriate `Recommendation` and present it in the `TestCompletedView` for the simple case of a single match and a single schedule preference. 
- Persisting which recommendation was shown for each attempt is required for analytics and follow-up, so a join/table is needed to record the mapping. 
- The UI advisor message should use the selected recommendation's `recommendedCourse`, `schedule`, and `startingDate` instead of hardcoded placeholders. 

### Description
- Added a new JPA entity `RecommendationMade` and repository `RecommendationMadeRepository` to store the mapping between an `Attempt` and the chosen `Recommendation`. 
- Added `RecommendationMadeService` to persist `RecommendationMade` records. 
- Extended `RecommendationRepository` with `findFirstByResultAndScheduleChosen(Result, Schedule)` to return a single matching recommendation for the simple scenario. 
- Updated `TestCompletedView` to resolve a recommendation from the attempt result and the student's first `schedulesPref`, persist the `RecommendationMade` record via `RecommendationMadeService`, and display `recommendedCourse`, `scheduleChosen`, and formatted `startingDate` in the advisor message. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.

------

## Description

  Rebrand the application from "Mask Overlay" to "Markly" and enhance the canvas preview experience with new zoom controls, auto-fit functionality, and automatic view adjustment when images are uploaded.

  ## Type of Change

  - [x] 🚀 **feat**: New feature

  ## Related Issues

  <!-- No related issues -->

  ## Changes Made

  **Rebranding (feat(rebrand)):**
  - Update all public-facing branding from "Mask Overlay" to "Markly"
  - Update landing page: hero title, feature cards, FAQ sections, footer copyright
  - Update navbar: brand name in both desktop and mobile views
  - Update page metadata: title and PWA app name for better discoverability
  - Update PWA manifest: app name and short name
  - Update GitHub links to SIAJI-Labs organization

  **Canvas Preview Enhancements (feat(canvas)):**
  - Add Fit to View button: Automatically scales image to 90% of available container space
  - Add Reset View button: Restores zoom to 100% with single click
  - Auto-fit on load: New images automatically fit to view when loaded (50ms delay)
  - Improve scaling logic: Simplified dimensions calculation using direct scale multiplication
  - High-resolution canvas: Canvas resolution matches scaled display dimensions for crisp rendering
  - Better font scaling: Text scaling consistent across all zoom levels
  - Refine zoom controls: 5% step size, 10% min, 150% max
  - Add scrollbar-hide utility: Hide scrollbars while maintaining drag-to-pan functionality
  - Focus on new files: Single uploads focus on that file, multiple uploads focus on first new file

  - [x] Tested locally with `npm run dev`
  - [x] Production build passes (`npm run build`)
  - [x] No linting errors (`npm run lint`)
  - [x] Tested zoom controls at 10%, 50%, 100%, 150%

  - [x] Tested auto-fit on image load

  - [x] Tested file focus behavior for single and multiple uploads

Removes all custom weapon and armor systems (to be remade later) and implements a new enemy pathfinding system with specific AI behavior types for target selection.

## Removed
- `armor/` directory (7 files) - ArmorPassive, ArmorRarity, CustomArmorPiece, CustomArmorSet, etc.
- `weapon/` directory (11 files) - CustomWeapon, WeaponAbility, WeaponRegistry, etc.
- Weapon data/model JSON files

## New AI Behavior System

| Behavior | Target Selection |
|----------|------------------|
| NORMAL | Closest player |
| RANGED | Keeps distance from player |
| RANGED_ADVANCED | Keeps distance, flees when too close |
| FLANKER | Stays outside line of sight until in range |
| ASSASSIN | Lowest HP player |
| BRUTE | Highest HP player |
| COWARD | Runs away below 20% HP |
| FAR_SIGHTED | Farthest player |
| CHAOTIC | Random player |

## Example Mobs
Nine mobs demonstrating each behavior, summonable via commands:

```
/summon rpgclasses_v2:grunt           # NORMAL
/summon rpgclasses_v2:skeleton_archer # RANGED
/summon rpgclasses_v2:elite_marksman  # RANGED_ADVANCED
/summon rpgclasses_v2:shadow_stalker  # FLANKER
/summon rpgclasses_v2:silent_blade    # ASSASSIN
/summon rpgclasses_v2:iron_goliath    # BRUTE
/summon rpgclasses_v2:goblin_scout    # COWARD
/summon rpgclasses_v2:eagle_eye       # FAR_SIGHTED
/summon rpgclasses_v2:chaos_imp       # CHAOTIC
```

## Other Changes
- Created missing `CustomEntityRegistry.java`
- Targets include armor stands with `"player"` tag for testing
- Updated language file with new entity translations

body:
### Motivation
- Replace the legacy dashboard with a modern CRM-style workspace that shows updated KPIs and two charts matching the provided visual direction.  
- Provide a unified CRM hub and reports area to make commercial workflows (projects, services, invoices, tickets, quotes) more accessible.  
- Replace ad-hoc `$_SESSION` alert usage with a small, reusable flash system for consistent UI notifications.  
- Surface cross-module quick actions and prefill links to speed common flows (create invoice from service/project, create project for a client, open tickets, etc.).

### Description
- Added dashboard metrics in `app/controllers/DashboardController.php` (projects count, open tickets, `revenueTrend`, `ticketStatusSummary`) and passed them to the view.  
- Replaced the old dashboard view with a new layout in `app/views/dashboard/index.php`, added two charts (`revenueTrendChart` and `ticketStatusChart`) using Chart.js, and updated interactions to prefill client/project/service selectors.  
- Introduced flash helpers `flash()` and `consume_flash()` in `app/helpers.php`, render flash alerts in `app/views/layouts/main.php`, and replaced many `$_SESSION` success/error usages across controllers with `flash()` calls.  
- Added CRM controllers/views (`CrmController`, `app/views/crm/hub.php`, `app/views/crm/reports.php`), new routes (`crm/hub`, `crm/reports`), and refreshed styling in `assets/css/custom.css` to match the new palette and card/hero styles; also added various UX quick-action links (clients, projects, services, quotes, invoices, tickets) across views.

### Testing
- Launched the PHP development server with `php -S 0.0.0.0:8000`, which started successfully.  
- Ran a Playwright script that visited `http://127.0.0.1:8000/index.php?route=dashboard` and saved a full-page screenshot to `artifacts/dashboard-modern.png`, which completed successfully.  
- No automated backend unit tests were run as part of this change.  
- Manual verification: spot-checked dashboard rendering, Chart.js initialization, flash alerts rendering in the main layout, and a few quick-action flows (creating/redirect links) locally.

body:
💡 What: Implemented edge trace merging in `plot_2d_network`. Instead of creating one `go.Scatter` trace per edge (which leads to thousands of traces), the code now groups edges by color (using binning for continuous values like energy or depth) and merges them into a single trace per group using `np.nan` separators.

🎯 Why: Rendering thousands of individual traces in Plotly/Streamlit is a significant performance bottleneck, causing slow figure generation on the server and laggy interaction in the browser.

📊 Impact:
- Trace count reduced from N (e.g., 2000) to ~50.
- Generation time reduced from ~3.33s to ~1.90s (~43% faster) for 2000 edges.
- Browser rendering is much smoother due to reduced DOM elements.

🔬 Measurement:
Measured using `tests/benchmark_viz.py` (deleted after verification) with 2000 edges.
Before: 2002 traces, 3.33s.
After: 52 traces, 1.90s.

## Description

Implements automated quality checks in CI to normalize special characters and validate repository configuration files before builds.

## Changes

**New workflow**: `.github/workflows/quality-checks.yml`

- **Quote/dash normalization**: Converts curly quotes (`""`), fancy apostrophes (`''`), and en-dashes (`–`) to ASCII equivalents across all text files
- **JSON validation**: Verifies `package.json` syntax
- **Shell validation**: Syntax-checks `fix-repo.sh` and all scripts in `scripts/`
- **Docker Compose validation**: Validates `docker-compose.yml` config (creates temp `.env` to bypass parsing issues with special chars)
- **Build chain**: Frozen lockfile install → lint → build → test

**Triggers**: Pushes to `main` and PRs targeting `main`

## Testing

- [x] YAML syntax validated
- [x] All validation commands tested locally
- [x] Docker Compose validation works with temporary `.env` workaround

## Notes

Uses `docker-compose.yml` since `docker-compose.prod.yml` doesn't exist in repository. Test step allows failures per requirements (`pnpm test || true`).

> Implement a CI pipeline in the `Infamous-freight-enterprises` repository to perform the following quality checks and validations on each push or pull request:
> 
> 1. Normalize quotes and dashes across all files in the repository:
>    ```bash
>    LC_ALL=C sed -i '' 's/[“”]/"/g; s/[’]/'\''/g; s/[–]/--/g' **/*
>    ```
> 
> 2. Validate the `package.json` file:
>    ```bash
>    node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('package.json','utf8'))"

Failed to resolve entry for package "@attio-mcp/core"

// Skip in CI until @attio-mcp/core package is built in workflow

```

author: dylan-smith
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate/security/code-scanning/3](https://github.com/dylan-smith/CheckMate/security/code-scanning/3)

In general, the fix is to ensure that only authorized users can delete a template identified by the `id` parameter. This usually means either (1) enforcing that the current user is allowed to access/delete the specific `Template` instance (e.g., they are the owner), or (2) restricting the action to a privileged role (e.g., administrators) if arbitrary-resource management is acceptable for that role.

Because we must not change existing functionality more than necessary and we have no information about ownership fields on `Template`, the safest, minimal change is to protect the `DeleteTemplate` action with an `[Authorize]` attribute specifying an appropriate role (e.g., `"admin"`). This mirrors the “GOOD” ASP.NET Core example in the background section. Concretely, in `CheckMate.WebApi/Controllers/TemplatesController.cs`, add `using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;` at the top so we can use `[Authorize]`, and annotate the `DeleteTemplate` method with `[Authorize(Roles = "admin")]` directly above `[HttpDelete("{id}")]`. This leaves the logic of finding and deleting the template unchanged, while ensuring only users with the `admin` role can perform deletions.

body:
## 概要
Issue #6 の実装: ゲーム内通知のキューイングと表示管理システムを提供するプラグイン

## 実装内容

### 主要機能
- ✅ **通知キューイングシステム** - 複数の通知を優先度順に自動管理
- ✅ **優先度管理** - 4段階の優先度（低/通常/高/緊急）
- ✅ **フェードイン/アウト制御** - カスタマイズ可能なタイミング制御
- ✅ **通知タイプ** - 6種類のタイプ（情報/成功/警告/エラー/実績/カスタム）
- ✅ **GameInstanceSubsystem** - ゲーム全体で統一的に管理
- ✅ **Blueprint完全対応** - C++とBlueprintの両方で使用可能
- ✅ **カスタマイズ可能** - 独自の通知UIを作成可能

### 実装ファイル

#### コア実装
- `NotificationData.h` - 通知データ構造体と列挙型
- `NotificationWidget.h/.cpp` - カスタマイズ可能なウィジェット基底クラス
- `NotificationManager.h/.cpp` - GameInstanceSubsystemベースの管理システム
- `NotificationSystem.uplugin` - プラグイン定義
- `NotificationSystem.Build.cs` - ビルド設定

#### ドキュメント
- `README.md` - インストール手順と基本的な使用方法
- `Documentation/Usage.md` - 詳細な使用方法とサンプル
- `Documentation/API.md` - 完全なAPIリファレンス
- `Documentation/Examples.md` - 実用的なサンプルコード集

## 使用方法

### 1. プラグインの有効化
1. Edit > Plugins から "Notification System" を有効化
2. エディタを再起動

### 2. 通知ウィジェットの作成
Widget Blueprintを作成し、親クラスを`NotificationWidget`に設定

### 3. 通知の表示
```cpp
// Blueprint
Get Game Instance
└─ Get Subsystem (Notification Manager)
    └─ Show Simple Notification
        ├─ Title: "アイテム取得"
        ├─ Message: "体力ポーションを入手しました"
        ├─ Type: Success
        └─ Priority: Normal

// C++
UNotificationManager* Manager = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UNotificationManager>();
Manager->ShowSimpleNotification(
    FText::FromString(TEXT("アイテム取得")),
    FText::FromString(TEXT("体力ポーションを入手しました")),
    ENotificationType::Success,
    ENotificationPriority::Normal
);
```

## テスト方法
1. プラグインを有効化してエディタを再起動
2. Widget Blueprintを作成（親クラス: NotificationWidget）
3. Blueprintで通知表示をテスト

## 関連Issue
Closes #6

## Upgrade to Ruby 4.0.0

Upgrades the project to Ruby 4.0.0, released on December 25, 2025.

### Changes:
- ✅ Update `.ruby-version` to 4.0.0
- ✅ Update `Dockerfile` RUBY_VERSION to 4.0.0
- ✅ Ruby 4 includes **YJIT** (production-ready JIT) by default
- ℹ️ ZJIT remains experimental (not enabled)

### Bootsnap CI Fix:
- ✅ Temporarily disable bootsnap in CI via `DISABLE_BOOTSNAP=1`
- Addresses intermittent `[BUG] rb_sys_fail(opendir) - errno == 0` race condition
- Related to [Ruby Bug #20586](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/20586) (missing error handling in dir.c)
- Will re-enable after confirming Ruby 4.0 compatibility in production

### Ruby 4.0 Key Features:
- **YJIT**: Production-ready JIT compiler (enabled by default)
- **Ruby Box**: Experimental isolated namespaces
- **Ractor improvements**: More stable and performant

### References:
- [Ruby 4.0.0 Release Announcement](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2025/12/25/ruby-4-0-0-released/)

body:
### Motivation
- Usuários não devem precisar fornecer `cnpj_access` no momento do login; isso estava causando falhas legítimas de autenticação quando o CNPJ divergente era rejeitado. 
- Manter o CNPJ apenas como dado de cadastro é suficiente para o fluxo funcional atual. 
- Reduzir atrito no login e evitar bloqueios indevidos por comparação adicional de CNPJ. 
- Corrigir discrepâncias entre cliente e servidor sobre o payload de autenticação.

### Description
- Removi a normalização e a verificação de CNPJ do `loginHandler` em `Backend/server.js`, e ajustei a validação inicial para exigir apenas `email` e `password` (`normalizedCnpj` e o bloco de comparação foram removidos). 
- Atualizei o cliente para enviar apenas `email` e `password` no endpoint de login em `api.ts`. 
- Ajustei a UI em `views/LoginView.tsx` para ocultar o campo de CNPJ no formulário de login (mantendo o campo para o fluxo de registro) e melhorar a exibição de mensagens de erro. 
- Atualizei a documentação na UI (`views/DocumentationView.tsx`) e textos de endpoint para refletir autenticação por e‑mail e senha.

### Testing
- Inicializei o front-end em modo dev com `npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4173`, e o servidor Vite iniciou corretamente (dev server pronto). 
- Rodei um script automatizado de Playwright para abrir a UI e gerar um screenshot, confirmando que o formulário de login não mostra o campo de CNPJ e o artefato foi gerado com sucesso. 
- Nenhum teste automatizado de backend (unit/integration) foi executado; a mudança no `loginHandler` precisa ser validada contra o banco de dados em execução. 
- Recomendo testar o login pós‑deploy com um request como `curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3333/auth/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"...","password":"..."}'` para verificar comportamento final contra o ambiente real.

### Motivation
- Resolve a runtime `SyntaxError` caused by the duplicated identifier `mEach` that prevented the app from parsing and running.
- Reduce UI fragility by preventing duplicate DOM nodes and avoiding crashes when optional debug elements are missing.
- Improve observability so recompute status and dedupe actions are visible in diagnostics.

### Description
- Renamed local pellet-mass variables to avoid repeated identifier declaration (`pelletEachMass`, `pelletEachInputMass`, `pelletEachMassLive`, etc.) and updated all call sites in `runSimulation`, event handling, and UI text updates to use the new names.
- Added `setRecomputeBubbleState(state, meta)` to centralize recompute status updates and extended `DEBUG_STATE` with fields to capture recompute metadata and missing-element flags.
- Added `dedupeAppNodes()` to remove duplicate `.wrap` containers, extra `.card` elements, and duplicated element IDs at init, and record results in `DEBUG_STATE.dedupeReport`.
- Hardened UI fallbacks by creating missing containers (e.g. `#flags`, `#chemTags`) and adjusted plotting/chemistry plumbing to consistently use cumulative chemistry arrays for rendering.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test` which executes `node scripts/validate-js.js` and it passed.
- Verified with a repository search that the old identifier is gone using `rg -n "\bmEach\b"` which returned no hits.

body:
Implements a comments feature allowing readers to engage with blog posts through a threaded discussion system.

## Database

- `comments` table with foreign key to `blog_posts`, indexed on `post_id`, `created_at`, `is_deleted`
- Soft delete support for moderation
- Migration script: `npm run db:migrate-comments`

## API

- `POST /api/comments` - Creates comment with validation (email format, 2000 char limit)
- `GET /api/comments?postId={id}` - Returns non-deleted comments ordered by newest first

author: copilot
body:
Stack pointer initialization issues in bare-metal RISC-V test executables prevented reliable string echo functionality via FIFO. Investigated using `riscv_rt` crate to provide proper runtime initialization and debugged the echo failure.

## Changes

### riscv_rt Integration
- Added `riscv-rt` v0.17.0 dependency with required linker infrastructure
- Created `memory.x` defining RAM region at 0x80000000 with proper section aliases
- Modified `build.rs` to emit `cargo:rustc-link-arg` directives for linker scripts
- Replaced manual `_start` with `#[entry]` macro for standards-compliant initialization
- Build works with standard cargo commands: `cargo build --release --bin hello_world`

### Echo Implementation
- Modified `hello_world.rs` to read from RX FIFO and echo to TX FIFO using a loop (max 50 iterations)
- Supports variable-length strings by reading until null terminator is encountered
- Updated test to use longer random pattern string: `"Qu1ck_Br0wn-F0x!Jump5*0v3r@Lazy#D0g$2024%"` (43 characters requiring 11 words)
- This provides a more challenging test that requires multiple read/write loop iterations

### Critical Bug Fix
**Root cause identified via instruction trace**: The simulator in `cpu-sim/src/sim.rs` was calling `bus.read_word(dmem_addr)` unconditionally on every instruction to populate `dmem_rdata`, even for store instructions.

**Impact**: When executing store instructions to FIFO DATA register (0x40000000):
1. Simulator would spuriously READ from FIFO (consuming a word from RX queue)
2. Then perform the actual WRITE to FIFO (with data from CPU register)
3. Result: RX queue drained faster than expected, wrong words echoed

**Fix**: Modified simulator to only read when `dmem_we == 0` (not a write instruction):
```rust
let rdata = if self.cpu.dmem_we == 0 {
    self.bus.read_word(dmem_addr)
} else {
    0 // For stores, rdata is not used by the CPU and should not trigger side effects
};
```

This prevents spurious reads with side effects on memory-mapped I/O devices like FIFOs.

## Test Status
- All 34 tests pass (including echo test)
- Echo test successfully validates: `"Qu1ck_Br0wn-F0x!Jump5*0v3r@Lazy#D0g$2024%"` → `"Qu1ck_Br0wn-F0x!Jump5*0v3r@Lazy#D0g$2024%"` ✓
- No clippy warnings
- Echo completes in ~226 cycles (processing 11 words across multiple loop iterations)

The issue was **not** stack initialization as initially suspected, but a simulator bug affecting any memory-mapped I/O with side effects on read operations.

## Summary
Fixes windowrule/layerrule syntax for Hyprland 0.53 compatibility.

## Changes
Hyprland 0.53 introduced breaking changes to windowrule syntax:

- `class:pattern` → `match:class pattern`
- `float` → `float on`
- `nofocus` → `no_focus on`
- `noborder` → `border_size 0`
- `noanim` → `animation none`
- `layerrule = noanim, X` → `layerrule = animation none, match:namespace X`
- `new_window_takes_over_fullscreen` → `on_focus_under_fullscreen`

author: sugoiii
body:
### Motivation

- Prevent crashes and undefined behavior when VBA callers pass null pointers, NaN/Inf or out-of-range numeric values into the Excel bridge APIs.
- Ensure arrays that are paired with counts are validated before dereferencing (e.g., pillar arrays, fixing arrays, bucket tenor arrays).
- Detect invalid/negative date serials and invalid numeric inputs (rates/notional/spreads/floor/bumps) early and produce clear, user-facing errors.
- Provide a consistent failure path that zeroes outputs and returns NaN while setting `lastError` for Excel clients.

### Description

- Added centralized helpers `isFiniteNumber`, `validateFinite`, `validatePositiveSerial`, `validateNonEmptyString`, and `fillHolidayDates` to validate inputs before use.
- Hardened `fromExcelSerial` to return an empty `Date` for non-finite or non-positive serials and validated each pillar/fixing/bucket date and numeric value in `fillCurveInput`, `fillFixings`, `fillLeg`, `fillBucketConfig`, and `buildPricingContext`.
- Guarded pointer array dereferences and checked `tenorStrings[i]` and index name presence; required curve/fixing/bucket pointers when counts > 0.
- Added `failAndReturnNaN` and wired it into `IRS_PRICE_AND_BUCKETS` so failures set `lastError`, call `zeroBuckets`, and return `NaN` consistently.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.
- The change set modifies `src/Excel.cpp` to add validations and a centralized failure path; please run existing unit/CI tests to verify behavior in your environment.

author: mmatera
body:
This is another step in making the formatting more compatible with WMA. This time, in adjusting how numbers are formatted in different forms and representations. 

I tried to stick to the form in which WMA does it, with a detail: Except in `OutputForm`, PrecisionReal numbers in WMA are shown with all the decimal places included in the internal representation. For example,
```
In[1]:= N[Pi,4]//InputForm                                                      

Out[1]//InputForm= 3.1415926535897932385`4.
```
In Mathics, because of our internal representation, ```N[Pi,4]``` results in a number with exactly 5 decimal digits  (`3.1416`4`) 

Apart from this difference,  the references for the tests were collected from WMA.

In order to make this work, some bugs and misimplementations were fixed:
* `RowBox.elements` now stores a `ListExpression` instead of the `RobBox.items` directly.
* `String.make_boxes` uses the internal value `String._value` instead of the proxy `String.value`.
* A more sophisticated analysis is used to determine when parenthesize the index in a `SuperscriptBox` in its `text` representation.

author: evanhyd
body:
<!--NOTE: Please make sure to read the contributing guidelines before submitting your pull request. There is a high chance your PR will be rejected or take a long time to be merged if you don't follow the guidelines. Thank you for your understanding - and thanks for taking the time to contribute!!-->

## Description
Extend the maximum possible teleportation range from 10 to 22 < sqrt(500) in vanilla minecraft.

In ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleMovePlayer(ServerboundMovePlayerPacket), the server checks if the player moves too fast in the following code:
```java
boolean flag = this.player.isFallFlying();
if (serverlevel.tickRateManager().runsNormally()) {
    this.receivedMovePacketCount++;
    int i = this.receivedMovePacketCount - this.knownMovePacketCount;
    if (i > 5) {
        LOGGER.debug("{} is sending move packets too frequently ({} packets since last tick)", this.player.getPlainTextName(), i);
        i = 1;
    }

    if (this.shouldCheckPlayerMovement(flag)) {
        float f2 = flag ? 300.0F : 100.0F;
        if (d10 - d9 > f2 * i) {
            LOGGER.warn("{} moved too quickly! {},{},{}", this.player.getPlainTextName(), d6, d7, d8);
            this.teleport(
                this.player.getX(),
                this.player.getY(),
                this.player.getZ(),
                this.player.getYRot(),
                this.player.getXRot()
            );
            return;
        }
    }
}
```

When the server receives multiple packets in a single tick, it will increment the "i" counter and ensures that the change in position is no longer than f2 * i, where f2 is a constant upper bound that's either sqrt(100) or sqrt(300) if flying with elytra.
By burst sending 5 packets in a single tick, it boosts up i to a maximum of 5 before resets. This allows us to increase the last packet's velocity to sqrt(100 * 5) or sqrt(300 * 5) without getting teleported back by the anti cheat.

## Testing
Try to teleport at least 20 blocks away, but no more than 22 blocks. Ensure there's no obstruction between the source and the destination, otherwise it will trigger other part of anticheat related to obstruction.

## References
This uses the same mechanics as the arrow damage and the mace damage hack.

author: flwrian
body:
## Title
**Search optimizations: move ordering, history heuristic fix, repetition bias, and stalemate handling**

---

## Description

This PR merges the `fix-stalemate` branch into `searchxp` and introduces several **search-level optimizations and cleanups** that improve both **performance** and **playing strength**, without modifying the evaluation function.

---

## Summary of changes

### 1. Move ordering overhaul
- Replaced quadratic bubble sort with **bucket-based move ordering**:
  - Transposition Table move first
  - Captures ordered by MVV-LVA
  - Quiet moves ordered by history heuristic
- Optimized `orderQMoves` using insertion sort on MVV-LVA scores
- Removed redundant score recomputation and unnecessary comparisons

**Result:** better cutoffs, higher effective depth, and improved NPS.

---

### 2. History heuristic fix
- Fixed incorrect history update logic where moves starting at zero would never accumulate value
- Implemented a proper **depth²-based, damped update**, equivalent to the Python reference implementation

**Result:** the history table now actually learns and improves quiet move ordering.

---

### 3. Repetition handling adjustment
- Reduced repetition draw bias from `-50` to `-5`
- Prevents overly defensive behavior and premature draw avoidance
- Keeps repetition pruning lightweight and consistent with expected engine behavior

---

### 4. Stalemate handling cleanup
- Removed redundant early stalemate detection
- Stalemate is now handled uniformly when no legal moves are available
- Prevents premature cutoffs of winning lines

---

### 5. Transposition Table mate score handling
- Corrected TT score unpacking to account for ply distance when probing
- Ensures consistent mate-distance behavior throughout the search

---

## Results

Self-play testing at **8.0+0.08** shows a **statistically significant Elo gain**:

- **fix-stalemate vs previous searchxp**
  - LLR: **+3.40**
  - Clear win rate advantage

- **All combined optimizations vs baseline**
  - LLR: **+3.16** over 2000+ games

All gains come purely from **search improvements** (no evaluation changes).

---

## Notes
- No evaluation parameters were modified
- No rule-based features (e.g. 50-move rule) were added
- Changes focus strictly on search correctness, pruning quality, and raw performance

---

This PR provides a cleaner, faster, and more stable search foundation for future improvements (killers, LMR, futility pruning, etc.).

body:
## Description

Implements Phase 2 of FCM integration - complete Firebase Cloud Messaging service with token management, permissions, and background message handling following MIP-05 privacy approach.

### Changes

- **FCMService class** - Token generation, storage, and refresh with `SharedPreferencesAsync`
- **Background handler** - Wakes app to process new events via existing `flutter_background_service`
- **Permission handling** - Request notification permissions on Android/iOS
- **Platform detection** - Skip Firebase on Linux (not supported)
- **Firebase initialization** - `Firebase.apps.isEmpty` check to prevent double initialization
- **Lazy messaging instance** - Getter pattern for `FirebaseMessaging.instance`
- **Riverpod provider** - Dependency injection for [FCMService](cci:2://file:///home/andrea/Documents/oss/mostrop2p/mobile/lib/services/fcm_service.dart:59:0-272:1)
- **Main.dart integration** - Initialize FCM on startup with error handling
- **Debug logging** - Essential logs for initialization tracking

### How to Test

#### 1. View FCM Initialization Logs

Run the app and monitor logs:

```bash
# Terminal 1: Run the app
fvm flutter run -d <android-device>

# Terminal 2: Monitor FCM logs
adb logcat -s flutter:I | grep "FCM:"
```

**Expected output:**
```
FCM: Starting initialization...
FCM: Firebase initialized (or "Firebase already initialized")
FCM: Notification permissions granted
FCM: Token obtained
FCM: Initialized successfully
```

#### 2. Token Generation

Verify token is generated and stored:

```bash
# Check if token exists in SharedPreferences
adb shell run-as network.mostro.app cat /data/data/network.mostro.app/shared_prefs/FlutterSharedPreferences.xml | grep fcm_token
```

**Expected:** Token string present in preferences

#### 3. Permissions

- **First launch:** Permission dialog should appear
- **Grant permissions:** App continues normally, logs show `FCM: Notification permissions granted`
- **Deny permissions:** App continues normally, logs show `FCM: Notification permissions not granted`

#### 4. Background Handler

Test background message handling:

1. Put app in background or close it
2. Send test notification from Firebase Console (or push server in Phase 3)
3. Check logs for background handler execution

**Expected:** No crashes, background service triggered

#### 5. Linux Compatibility

```bash
fvm flutter run -d linux
```

**Expected log:**
```
FCM: Skipping initialization on Linux (not supported)
```

App should launch normally without Firebase errors.

### Success Criteria

✅ App launches without errors  
✅ FCM initialization logs appear in correct order  
✅ Token generated and stored in SharedPreferences  
✅ Permissions requested on first launch  
✅ App continues if permissions denied  
✅ No crashes on background messages  
✅ Linux compatibility maintained (Firebase skipped)  
✅ No double initialization errors  

### Notes

- This PR implements **Phase 2 only** - token registration with push server (Phase 3) is not included
- FCM tokens are stored locally but not yet sent to the notification server
- Background handler integrates with existing `flutter_background_service` (no duplication)
- Silent push notifications (no content) will be used in production

## Summary

- **Throttled output batching**: Buffer WebSocket output chunks and flush every 100ms instead of updating Vue state on every chunk. This reduces reactivity overhead from hundreds of updates per second to ~10.
- **Output line limits**: Cap output at 2000 lines, trimming oldest lines when exceeded. Prevents memory bloat and DOM slowdown with large outputs.
- **Truncation warning UI**: Shows warning banner when output is truncated so users know they're seeing partial output.

## Problem

The command button output tab had two issues:
1. Output stops showing after a while (memory exhaustion from unbounded output)
2. UI becomes sluggish during streaming (excessive Vue reactivity from per-chunk updates)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (50 tests in commandButtons.test.js)
- [x] Full test suite passes (1340+ web tests, 1417+ server tests)
- [ ] Manual test: Run a command that generates rapid output (e.g., `seq 1 10000`) and verify UI stays responsive

body:
Implements a mobile usability pass for the Telegram Mini App poker game, addressing typography readability, touch target compliance, ActionBar/seat overlap, and adding haptic feedback.

### Typography & Touch Targets
- Raised minimum font sizes in design tokens (10px→11px, 12px→13px, etc.)
- Added `--touch-target-min: 44px` CSS variable
- ActionBar buttons increased to min-height 44px
- Slider thumb enlarged from 22px to 32px

### ActionBar Overlap Fix
- Added `--action-bar-height` and `--action-bar-total-offset` CSS variables
- Table screen reserves bottom padding to prevent seat/ActionBar overlap

### Responsive Seat Sizing
- PlayerSeat uses `clamp()` for viewport-adaptive sizing
- Added `--seat-scale-factor` CSS variable with media query breakpoints

```tsx
// PlayerSeat now scales responsively
style={{
  width: isHorizontal 
    ? `calc(clamp(85px, 12vw, 110px) * var(--seat-scale-factor, 1))` 
    : `calc(clamp(75px, 10vw, 95px) * var(--seat-scale-factor, 1))`,
}}
```

### Haptic Feedback
- New `useHapticFeedback` hook wrapping Telegram WebApp SDK (safe no-op outside Telegram)
- Integrated with ActionBar actions; throttled for slider adjustments

### Files Changed
- `src/styles/design-tokens.css` – typography scale, touch target vars
- `src/styles/table-layout.css` – ActionBar spacing, seat responsiveness
- `src/styles/mobile.css` – touch target rules
- `src/index.css` – slider thumb sizing
- `src/legacy/ui/table-legacy/table/ActionBar.tsx` – touch targets, haptics
- `src/legacy/ui/table-legacy/table/PlayerSeat.tsx` – responsive clamp() sizing
- `src/hooks/useHapticFeedback.ts` – new file

### Safety Notes
No changes to Table.tsx game logic, WebSocket connections, or action submission. RTL/Farsi support preserved.

![Home page landscape](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04d4826d-dfe3-4f66-b30c-208169eccf2a)

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

You are a Senior Frontend Engineer + Mobile UX specialist for a Telegram Mini App poker game.

Context you must respect (from repo analysis report):
- Frontend: React 18 + Vite 5 + TypeScript
- Styling: Tailwind CSS + CSS variables (design-tokens.css) + some page CSS files
- State: Zustand + multiple Context Providers (Telegram, Theme, Localization, etc.)
- Mobile-first, landscape-only enforced via OrientationGuard
- Telegram Mini App SDK integration exists
- High-risk: Table.tsx is ~2600+ lines and tightly coupled to WebSocket/game logic. Avoid risky changes.
- Target improvements: ActionBar overlap, touch targets, typography scale, seat/table responsiveness, slider usability, haptics, and perceived performance.

Your task:
Implement a UI/UX improvement pass that upgrades mobile usability and visual consistency WITHOUT breaking gameplay.

Hard rules:
1) Do NOT guess file paths. Discover them from the repository.
2) Do NOT refactor game logic or WebSocket logic.
3) Prefer CSS/layout/component-level changes over rewriting Table.tsx.
4) Keep changes incremental, reviewable, and reversible.
5) Keep RTL/Farsi support intact (don’t hardcode LTR-only layouts).
6) Avoid new heavy dependencies. If you add anything, justify it and keep it minimal.

========================
PHASE 0 — INVENTORY (READ ONLY)
========================
- Locate and open:
  - design tokens file (design-tokens.css)
  - Table.tsx and the table subcomponents (PlayerSeat, ActionBar, community board, etc.)
  - layout components (MainLayout, OrientationGuard)
  - any existing table layout CSS (table-layout.css / mobile.css / animations.css etc.)
- Output a short "FILES FOUND" list with exact paths you discovered.

========================
PHASE 1 — QUICK WINS (SAFE, LOW RISK)
========================
Goal: Improve readability + touch targets across the app with minimal code risk.

A) Typography baseline
- Introduce a sane minimum mobile font scale:
  - Prefer design tokens / tailwind config approach (if present) or shared utility classes.
  - Raise common 9–12px usage to more readable sizes where it affects critical UI (names, balances, action labels).
  - Ensure truncation has proper ellipsis and doesn’t hide key info.
- Keep layouts from overflowing. Use clamp() or responsive tailwind classes where appropriate.

B) Touch target compliance
- Ensure primary interactive elements meet >=44px height/size on mobile:
  - Action bar primary actions
  - table navigation/back/menus
  - key lobby/home CTAs
- Use padding + min-h + gap tuning (not massive redesign).

Deliverable for Phase 1:
- Implement changes
- Provide a list: “What changed” + “Why safe”
- List exact files modified

========================
PHASE 2 — TABLE UI FIXES (MEDIUM RISK, STILL SAFE)
========================
Goal: Fix the most painful table usability issues WITHOUT rewriting game logic.

A) ActionBar overlap
- Ensure the ActionBar does NOT obscure player seats or critical table content.
- Implement a robust solution:
  - Add safe-area padding for notched devices
  - Ensure table content has bottom inset / padding equal to action bar height
  - Prefer CSS layout approach (e.g., container padding, sticky area, reserved space) rather than changing game state logic.

B) Seat sizing and responsiveness
- PlayerSeat is currently fixed-size; update it to scale with viewport and table container:
  - Use CSS variables or clamp() so seats adapt across common phone sizes.
  - Prevent seat overlap on narrow viewports.
  - Maintain the “hero player at bottom” concept and current rotation behavior.
- Any seat-positioning changes should be done in CSS/layout helpers where possible.

C) Raise slider usability
- Improve the raise interaction:
  - Increase slider thumb hit area (>=44px effective)
  - Add preset buttons (e.g., 1/2 pot, pot, all-in) ONLY if you can do it without touching core action submission logic.
  - Keep existing slider functionality; presets should just set the slider value.

D) Haptic feedback (Telegram-safe)
- Add subtle haptics on primary actions if Telegram SDK provides it (or safely no-op if not available).
- Must not throw errors outside Telegram container.

Deliverable for Phase 2:
- Implement changes
- Add a short “Table safety notes” section explaining how you avoided breaking game logic.
- List exact files changed.

========================
PHASE 3 — PERFORMANCE / POLISH (OPTIONAL, LOW RISK)
========================
Goal: Reduce perceived jank and improve smoothness without changing core animations logic.
- Audit any heavy animations (chips fly, confetti, timers).
- Prefer:
  - reducing unnecessary re-renders (memo where safe)
  - CSS transform-based animations
  - respecting prefers-reduced-motion if available
- Do NOT redesign animations; just prevent obvious jank.

========================
QUALITY GATES (MUST PASS)
========================
Before finalizing, verify:
- Build passes (npm run build / pnpm build depending on repo)
- No TypeScript errors
- No obvious U...

</details>

body:
Implements two endpoints for email verification flow: verifying codes sent during registration and resending codes on demand. Includes user microservice RPC handlers to support the verification workflow.

## Endpoints

**POST `/auth/verify-email`**
- Validates 6-digit code against email
- Single-use tokens, differentiated expired vs invalid errors
- Updates user `pending` → `active` via RPC to user service, emits `user.verified` event
- Returns 409 for already-verified users

**POST `/auth/resend-verification`**
- Rate limited: 3 attempts/hour (configurable via `VERIFICATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `VERIFICATION_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW`)
- Returns success for non-existent users (anti-enumeration)
- Invalidates previous codes, generates new 6-digit token
- Gracefully handles notification service failures

## Implementation

**Auth Service:**

**DTOs**: `verify-email.dto.ts`, `resend-verification.dto.ts` with class-validator annotations

**Service methods**:
```typescript
async verifyEmail(data: VerifyEmailDto) {
  // Checks token validity, differentiates expired vs invalid
  // Marks token as used, updates user status via RPC
  // Emits user.verified event
}

async resendVerification(data: ResendVerificationDto) {
  // Enforces rate limits, soft-fails for non-existent users
  // Generates new token, sends via notification RPC
}
```

**Repository**: Added `findToken()` to distinguish expired from invalid codes

**User Service:**

**RPC Handlers**: Added to support email verification workflow
- `updateUserStatus` - Updates user status and verifiedAt timestamp via email lookup
- `updateLastLogin` - Updates lastLoginAt timestamp

**Repository Updates**: Added `verifiedAt` to UpdateUserDto interface

**TypeScript Config**: Added `resolveJsonModule` to support JSON imports

**Error handling**: New `AUTH_0009` (409) for already-verified users, localized en/vi

**Events**: `AUTH_USER_VERIFIED` routing key for downstream services

## Configuration

```bash
VERIFICATION_TOKEN_TTL=15           # minutes
VERIFICATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3
VERIFICATION_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW=3600000  # ms
```

## Testing

> <issue_title>✅ Issue: API xác thực email & API gửi lại mã xác thực</issue_title>
> <issue_description>### 📌 Yêu cầu chính
> - **Mục tiêu**: Thêm 2 API trong `auth` service:
>   1. API xác thực email bằng mã xác thực đã gửi khi đăng ký.
>   2. API gửi lại mã xác thực tới email đã đăng ký (người dùng chỉ cần nhập email).
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🧩 Yêu cầu chi tiết
> 
> #### 1) API xác thực email
> - **Endpoint**: POST `/auth/verify-email`
> - **Request body**:
>   ```json
>   {
>     "email": "user@example.com",
>     "code": "123456"
>   }
>   ```
> - **Behavior**:
>   - Kiểm tra mã hợp lệ, khớp với mã đã lưu và chưa hết hạn.
>   - Mã là một lần dùng (single-use) — sau verify xóa/mark as used.
>   - Khi verify thành công: cập nhật `user.status = verified` (hoặc tương đương), emit event `user.verified`, trả 200 và thông tin tối thiểu (userId, email, message).
>   - Nếu mã sai/hết hạn → trả lỗi chuẩn (ví dụ `VALIDATION_...` hoặc `AUTH_CODE_EXPIRED`) kèm info trong `details`.
>   - Nếu email chưa đăng ký → trả 404 hoặc lỗi chuẩn (không tiết lộ nhiều).
> - **Edge cases**:
>   - Nếu user đã verified → trả 409 Conflict hoặc 200 idempotent với message "already verified".
>   - Log & metric: `verification.success` / `verification.failure`.
> 
> #### 2) API gửi lại mã xác thực (resend)
> - **Endpoint**: POST `/auth/resend-verification`
> - **Request body**:
>   ```json
>   {
>     "email": "user@example.com"
>   }
>   ```
> - **Behavior**:
>   - Xác thực email đã đăng ký và user chưa verified.
>   - Sinh mã mới hoặc reuse (kèm refresh expiry) tùy policy; luôn rate-limit để tránh spamming.
>   - Gửi email chứa mã (hoặc link) qua SMTP; dùng template giống flow đăng ký.
>   - Trả 200 cùng message "verification sent" hoặc thông tin lượt gửi (ví dụ remaining tries).
>   - Nếu email chưa đăng ký → trả 404 hoặc 200 (soft response) để tránh lộ tồn tại tài khoản (configurable).
> - **Rate limiting & abuse control**:
>   - Giới hạn số lần gửi (e.g., max 3 resend / 1 giờ).
>   - Throttling IP/email; log suspicious patterns.
>   - Thêm CAPTCHA hoặc verification challenge nếu nghi ngờ lạm dụng (optional).
> - **Security**:
>   - Không gửi mã cùng lúc cho từng request vượt limit.
>   - Không tiết lộ sensitive info trong response.
>   - Use SMTP config from env; support testing via Ethereal / mock SMTP.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### ✅ Tiêu chí chấp nhận (Acceptance Criteria)
> - [ ] POST `/auth/verify-email` với email + code hợp lệ → trả 200, user marked verified, `user.verified` event emitted.
> - [ ] POST `/auth/verify-email` với code hết hạn hoặc sai → trả lỗi có `errorCode` & `details` mô tả.
> - [ ] POST `/auth/resend-verification` với email chưa verified → gửi email thành công (kiểm tra qua mock/Ethereal) và trả 200.
> - [ ] Giới hạn resend (ví dụ 3/1h) được enforced và tested.
> - [ ] Unit tests cho logic verify + resend.
> - [ ] Integration tests: simulate register → receive code → verify; resend flow tested.
> - [ ] Logs/metrics: counts for success/failure/resend attempts exist.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### ⚙️ Env / Config (mẫu)
> - `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `AUTH_EMAIL_FROM`
> - `VERIFICATION_CODE_TTL` (ví dụ 15m)
> - `VERIFICATION_CODE_LENGTH` (6)
> - `VERIFICATION_RESEND_LIMIT` (e.g., 3)
> - `VERIFICATION_RESEND_WINDOW` (e.g., 3600 seconds)
> 
> ---
> 
> ### 🧪 Tests & Validation
> - Unit tests for:
>   - code generation, storage, expiry logic.
>   - single-use behavior (cannot reuse code).
>   - rate-limiter logic.
> - Integration tests:
>   - Use `mongodb-memory-server` or test DB + mock SMTP (ethereal) to confirm email sent.
>   - End-to-end: signup → verify code flows.

body:
### Motivation
- Use a large model to generate diverse, natural replacement candidates for bracketed phrases in Step3 while keeping replacements controllable and reproducible.
- Ensure bracketed object phrases are full noun phrases (merge/expand nearby color/material/texture modifiers) so a single object is replaced consistently.
- Apply a centralized fuzzy-word normalization stage after model generation to remove/normalize vague modifiers (including `smooth`) and avoid vague color qualifiers.
- Preserve robot-related descriptions by excluding robot keywords from bracketing and replacement flows and align parent/child phrase replacements for consistency.

### Description
- Added LLM prompt templates and clause-splitting support via `PRE2_SPLIT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` and `DESCRIPTOR_EXTRACT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`, plus `step2_prepare_clause_context` to obtain clause-separated context for robot filtering.
- Implemented bracket expansion with `expand_bracketed_prompt` (merges adjacent descriptor tokens into larger noun-phrase brackets while avoiding robot/verb tokens) and added `_descriptor_token` / `_noun_modifier_token` helpers.
- Reworked Step3 replacement generation in `step3_generate_replacements_json` to: call the model for JSON replacements, cache LLM outputs (`_step3_cache_path`), normalize/clean candidates with `_normalize_replacement_phrase`, filter vague/robot terms, and enforce parent/child alignment so longer (parent) phrases drive shorter (child) replacements.
- Introduced fuzzy-word handling constants and utilities: added `VAGUE_TEXTURE_MODIFIERS` (contains `smooth`), `is_vague_color_phrase`, and color-bias splitting `_split_color_bias`, and updated README changelog and wordlist maintenance guidance to document these changes.

### Testing

body:
## Summary

This PR adds three major features to mcp-local-rag:

### 1. `ingest_data` Tool
- Ingest raw content directly (HTML, text, markdown) without requiring a file path
- Supports web pages fetched via LLM or browser MCP tools
- Preserves original source URL for reference in search results
- Raw data stored in `{DB_PATH}/raw-data/` for re-processing capability

### 2. HTML Parser
- Extracts main content using Mozilla Readability (removes navigation, ads, boilerplate)
- Converts to Markdown via Turndown for consistent chunking
- Preserves document structure (headings, lists, code blocks)

### 3. Agent Skills (Agent Skills Standard)
- Skills for Claude Code, Codex, and other AI assistants supporting [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/)
- Query optimization guidance (expansion patterns, score interpretation)
- Result refinement patterns (when to synthesize vs filter)
- HTML ingestion workflow
- Installable via `npx mcp-local-rag-skills`

## Changes

| Area | Files | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| MCP Server | `src/server/index.ts` | Add `ingest_data` tool, source restoration in results |
| Raw Data | `src/server/raw-data-utils.ts` | URL normalization, base64 encoding, file storage |
| HTML Parser | `src/parser/html-parser.ts` | Readability + Turndown pipeline |
| Skills | `skills/mcp-local-rag/` | SKILL.md + references for RAG optimization |
| Installer | `src/bin/install-skills.ts` | npx installer for multiple targets |
| Tests | `src/__tests__/` | Unit tests for all new components |
| Docs | `README.md` | Usage documentation updates |

## Design Decisions

- **No schema changes**: `ingest_data` saves to raw-data dir then calls existing `ingest_file` internally
- **MCP stays simple**: Advanced RAG techniques (reranking, query rewriting) delegated to LLM via Skills
- **Skills follow standard**: Compatible with Claude Code, Codex, VS Code Copilot

author: arustydev
body:
## Summary

This PR adds the `convert-python-roc` skill for translating Python code to idiomatic Roc. The skill extends `meta-convert-dev` with Python-to-Roc specific patterns, addressing the unique challenges of converting from a dynamic, GC-based runtime to a statically-typed, platform-separated functional language.

### Key Features

**Type System Coverage:**
- Comprehensive type mappings (primitives, collections, composite types)
- Dynamic → static type inference guidance
- Optional/None handling via tag unions
- Union types → discriminated unions

**Paradigm Translation:**
- OOP (classes) → functional (records + modules)
- Mutable by default → immutable by default
- Exceptions → Result types
- Asyncio → Task-based effects
- REPL-driven → expect-driven development

**Conversion Patterns:**
1. None/Optional handling
2. Result error handling
3. List comprehensions
4. Dictionary operations
5. String formatting
6. Class → Record + Module
7. Async/await → Task
8. Context managers
9. Exception hierarchy → tagged errors
10. Decorators → higher-order functions

**Platform Architecture:**
- Mental model shift: Python runtime → Roc platform model
- Pure vs effectful code separation
- Task-based effects system
- GIL considerations (parallelism benefits)

**Examples:**
- Simple: Optional handling
- Medium: Result error chaining
- Complex: Async file processing with platform Tasks

**Dev Workflow:**
- REPL translation (IPython/Jupyter → roc repl/expect)
- Testing (pytest → expect statements)
- Build system (pyproject.toml → platform URLs)

### 8 Pillars Validation

| Pillar | Python | Roc | Coverage |
|--------|--------|-----|----------|
| Module | ✓ | ✓ | Comprehensive |
| Error | ✓ | ✓ | Exception → Result translation |
| Concurrency | ✓ | ✓ | Asyncio → Task |
| Metaprogramming | ~ | ✓ | Decorators → HOF |
| Zero/Default | ✓ | ~ | Tag union patterns |
| Serialization | ✓ | ~ | Inferred from abilities |
| Build | ✓ | ~ | Platform-based |
| Testing | ✓ | ✓ | pytest → expect |
| Dev Workflow | ✓ | ~ | **9th pillar included** |

**Score:** 14.5/18 (Good) - Included 9th pillar for REPL workflow

### Quality Standards Met

### Unique Contributions

This skill uniquely addresses:

1. **Python's Dynamic Nature:** Explicit guidance on translating duck typing to static structural types
2. **REPL Workflow Loss:** Comprehensive dev workflow section (9th pillar) for developers transitioning from Python's strong REPL culture
3. **Platform Model:** Clear explanation of Roc's platform/application separation vs Python's unified runtime

author: elmorshedy-del
body:
### Motivation

- Historical Meta imports for Shawq sometimes store account-level totals under `country = 'ALL'`, which can cause double-counting when per-country rows also exist. 
- Funnel diagnostics and sparklines were summing per-country rows and therefore could show inflated spend compared to historical Meta totals. 
- The change aims to prefer the `country = 'ALL'` totals for Shawq when present, so dashboard cards and sparklines match historical Meta spend. 
- Make the fix minimally and locally inside the funnel diagnostics logic to avoid touching unrelated code paths.

### Description

- Updated `getFunnelDiagnostics` in `server/services/analyticsService.js` to detect whether `meta_daily_metrics` contains `country = 'ALL'` rows for the requested range and prefer those totals for Shawq. 
- Added `buildCountryClause` helper to construct a per-range country filter (returns `" AND country = 'ALL'"` when applicable) and applied it to current, previous and daily (sparkline) queries. 
- Reworked the query construction to use a `buildSummaryQuery` function so current and previous queries can use the appropriate per-range country clause. 
- Kept existing behavior for non-Shawq stores and preserved campaign filtering and status filtering logic unchanged.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed for this change. 
- The change was committed and the modified file is `server/services/analyticsService.js` and no other files were modified. 
- Code edits are localized and conservative: SQL clauses were composed to reuse existing parameters and avoid altering unrelated query logic. 
- Manual verification is recommended in a staging environment to confirm spend and sparkline totals now match historical Meta imports for Shawq.

author: shinoharaharuna
body:
### The Issue

After downloading and installing the `.deb` package from the latest release on **Kubuntu 24.04 LTS**, the application failed to launch via the GUI.

Running `Voquill` from the terminal revealed a missing shared library error regarding `libxdo`:

```bash
$ Voquill 
Voquill: error while loading shared libraries: libxdo.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The application relies on `rdev`/`enigo` (or similar crates for input simulation) which dynamically link to `libxdo`, but `libxdo3` was not listed as a package dependency in the generated Debian control file.

### Fix

I have updated `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.prod.conf.json` to explicitly include `libxdo3` in the linux bundle configuration.

### Environment

Testing was performed on the following machine:

* **OS:** Kubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (Noble Numbat)
* **Kernel:** Linux 6.8.0-79-generic
* **Architecture:** x86_64

### Verification

I built the package locally using `tauri build` with the prod config and verified the generated `.deb` metadata.

**Before (Official Release):**
```bash
$ dpkg-deb -I Voquill_0.0.245_amd64.deb | grep Depends
 Depends: libayatana-appindicator3-1, libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0
```

**After (This PR):**
```bash
$ dpkg-deb -I ../Code/voquill/apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/Voquill_0.1.0_amd64.deb | grep Depends 
 Depends: libxdo3, libayatana-appindicator3-1, libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0
```

The generated package now correctly declares `libxdo3` as a dependency, allowing `apt` to install it automatically.

body:
Review of Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Makefile, and API documentation revealed broken kustomize overlays and stale docs.

### Kubernetes Fixes

All three overlays (development, staging, production) were failing because they used `configMapGenerator` with `behavior: merge` against a raw ConfigMap resource in base.

**Before (broken):**
```yaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: vulcanami-config
    behavior: merge
    literals:
      - ENVIRONMENT=development
```

**After (working):**
```yaml
patches:
  - patch: |-
      apiVersion: v1
      kind: ConfigMap
      metadata:
        name: vulcanami-config
      data:
        ENVIRONMENT: "development"
        LOG_LEVEL: "DEBUG"
    target:

author: kevinz857
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

  /kind feature

  **What this PR does / why we need it**:

  This PR introduces multiple performance optimizations for the ResourceBinding to Work synchronization path, targeting large-scale Pod distribution scenarios (10000+ Pods).

  ### Background

  During stress testing with 12000+ Pods distributed to dual clusters, we observed:
  - Pods: 12649
  - ResourceBindings: 12645 (caught up)
  - **Works: 6646 (~6000 lagging behind)**

  The bottleneck was identified in the binding-controller's RB → Work synchronization path.

  ### Key Optimizations

  #### 1. AsyncWorkCreator for Binding Controller
  **File:** `pkg/controllers/binding/async_work_creator.go` (new)

  - Decouples Work creation from reconcile loop using configurable async workers (default: 64)
  - Implements **Assume Cache** pattern (borrowed from kube-scheduler's proven design)
  - Adds failure retry via requeue callback mechanism
  - Periodic cleanup of stale cache entries (every 5 min)

  #### 2. Parallel Work Preparation and Execution
  **File:** `pkg/controllers/binding/common.go`

  - Parallelizes DeepCopy and ApplyOverridePolicies across target clusters
  - Concurrent Work creation for multi-cluster scenarios
  - Single-cluster fast path to avoid goroutine overhead

  #### 3. CreateOrUpdateWork Optimization
  **File:** `pkg/controllers/ctrlutil/work.go`

  - Implements **Create-First** pattern (try Create before Get+Update)
  - Adds fast-path comparison to skip unchanged Work updates
  - Reduces API calls by 30-50% in update scenarios

  #### 4. Precise Orphan Work Detection
  **Files:** `pkg/controllers/binding/binding_controller.go`, `cluster_resource_binding_controller.go`

  - Uses `TargetClustersHashAnnotation` to track cluster changes
  - Skips orphan check when target clusters haven't changed
  - **Expected 90%+ reduction in List API calls**

  #### 5. AsyncBinder for Scheduler
  **File:** `pkg/scheduler/binder/binder.go` (new)

  - 32 async workers for RB/CRB patch operations
  - Decouples scheduling decisions from persistence

  ### New Configuration Options

  | Flag | Default | Component | Description |
  |------|---------|-----------|-------------|
  | `--enable-async-work-creation` | false | controller-manager | Enable async work creation |
  | `--async-work-workers` | 64 | controller-manager | Number of async workers |
  | `--enable-async-bind` | false | scheduler | Enable async binding |
  | `--async-bind-workers` | 32 | scheduler | Number of async bind workers |

  ### Performance Results

  #### API Call Reduction (per ResourceBinding, dual-cluster)

  | Operation | Before | After | Reduction |
  |-----------|--------|-------|-----------|
  | Orphan check (List) | 1 | 0 (when clusters unchanged) | **100%** |
  | Work Create | 2 (Get+Create) × 2 | 1 (Create) × 2 | **50%** |
  | Events | 2 | 0 | **100%** |
  | **Total API calls** | **8 (sequential)** | **3 (2 parallel)** | **62%** |

  #### Throughput Improvement

  With optimized code + proper configuration tuning:

  | Configuration | Before | After |
  |---------------|--------|-------|
  | `--rate-limiter-qps` | 10 | 1000+ |

author: suvorovrain
body:
# A lot of lanegg improvements
This PR brings following changes
## Cardinality cost function
Cost of the plan calculates by the following
rules:

`Label`:
We calculate in advice nnz of source matrix, nnz of source
matrix reduced by row and columns. We use these values
to calculate cost of the parent nodes. We assume that
`Label` nodes zero cost.

`Seq`:
We calculate the cost of `Seq` nodes based on the fact that
matrix multiplication can be viewed as a `JOIN` operation
from relation algebra. So for C = Seq(A,B) we have:

`cost(C) = cost(A) + cost(B) + cost(Seq)`

Where cost(Seq) can be compute by following way:

`cost(Seq) = nnz(A)*nnz(B)/max(nnz_r(A),nnz_c(B))`

where `nnz_r` is a nnz of reduced by rows matrix and
`nnz_c` is a nnz of reduced by columns matrix.

Estimates for nnz_r(C) and nnz_c(C) not ready at this
moment.
Estimates for nnz(C) are done by assuming that non zero
elemnts are distributed uniformly (usually this is
not true).

`Alt`:
We calculate the cost of `Alt` nodes based on assumption
that non zero values of A and B are independent sets.
So, for C = Alt(A,B)

`cost(C) = cost(A) + cost(B) + cost(Alt)`

Where `cost(Alt)` can be compute by following way:

`cost(Alt) = nnz(A) + nnz(B) - nnz(A)*nnz(B)/n^2`

Where n - dimension of squared matrix.

Estimates for nnz(C), nnz_r(C) and nnz_c(C) are done
by same assumptions.

'Star':
`Star` denotes a TC of source matrix, so it's very
expensive node. We give a huge penalty to this node
and at this moment assume that for C = A*:
nnz(C) = n^2, nnz_r(C) and nnz_c(C) = n.

`LStar` and `RStar`:
Our goal was make these nodes cheaper than `Star` node.
So we gave small penalty and use the same approach as
we used in `Seq` node estimation

## Interface improvement
Now user can choose one of the predefined cost functions by passing a command line argument. At this moment three parameters available:

1. `simple` --- run solver on raw plan without optimization
2. `cardinality` --- run solver on plan optimized via cardinality based cost function
3. `random` --- debug option for iterating over "all" possible plan and collecting data about best and worst plans (obviously, it's slow)

## Tests
Some end-to-end tests are provided in this pr.
We run our solver on different type of queries (any-any, con-any, any-con) with all available cost function (cardinality, simple) and compare result with result of originial [rpq-matrix](https://github.com/adriangbrandon/rpq-matrix) library on [RPQbench](https://github.com/Mamenglu/LD-RPQB/tree/main/dataset) dataset.
You can run tests via:
```
cargo test --release
```

## Input processing
Some very important improvements in input reading.

### Lazy matrix reading
Usually, we don't use all matrices from input dataset in querry, so we can use `LAGraph_MMRead` only when
matrix label appears in query. Before this PR **all** matrices was read before query evaluation and it was very slow. 

### now we read only first three lines of input matrix to get `nvals` value.
The `nvals` stored in third line of matrix_market file, so we don't need to read whole file to obtain this value.

## Debug
Detailed debug info in debug build.

### Execution and planning time
Now user can obtain detailed info about time that was spent on plan optimization

### Comparison with "best" plan for current query
User can compare plan that was obtained by specific cost function with "best" plan that was found with iterating over all possible plans

### plan pretty-printer
Add plan pretty printer. Example:
`Label(LabelMeta { name: "Taliyah_Jafari", nvals: 1, rreduce_nvals: 1, creduce_nvals: 1 }),
 Label(LabelMeta { name: "creator", nvals: 34264, rreduce_nvals: 3125, creduce_nvals: 20600 }),
 Seq([1, 0]), Label(LabelMeta { name: "cite", nvals: 2882, rreduce_nvals: 173, creduce_nvals: 107 }),
 Seq([3, 2]), Label(LabelMeta { name: "references", nvals: 173, rreduce_nvals: 161, creduce_nvals: 173 }), Seq([5, 4])`
turns into
`<references#173>/(<cite#2882>/(<creator#34264>/<Taliyah_Jafari#1>))`
## Other

- data catalog for input matrices (number of non-zero rows and columns in matrices)
- fix memory leaks for label matrices in query with constraints (we don't free label matrices in `LAGraph_RPQMatrix_Destroy`)

author: darwin808
body:
## Summary

- Throw a clear, actionable error when SlotMixin is used without a shadowRoot
- Fix flaky OverlayController test on Firefox

## SlotMixin Error Improvement

Previously, when SlotMixin was used in a component that overrides `createRenderRoot()` to return `this` (no shadow DOM), it would:
1. Log a vague `console.error('[SlotMixin] No shadowRoot was found')`
2. Continue executing and crash with a cryptic error later

Now it throws immediately with a helpful message:
```
[SlotMixin] SlotMixin requires a shadowRoot to render slots. 
Make sure your component has a shadowRoot (do not override createRenderRoot() to return 'this').
```

This helps developers quickly identify and fix the issue.

## Firefox Test Fix

The test "on [Escape] press in child overlay: parent hides, child stays shown" was flaky on Firefox CI.

**Root cause:** `sendKeys({ press: 'Escape' })` sends the keyboard event to the focused element. In Firefox headless mode, `element.focus()` can silently fail, causing the event to be dispatched to the wrong element. This made `event.composedPath()` not include the child's contentNode, so the `#outsideEscKeyHandler` incorrectly thought Escape was pressed "outside" and hid the child overlay.

**Fix:** Dispatch the `keyup` event directly on the target element instead of relying on focus + `sendKeys`. This ensures correct `event.target` and `event.composedPath()` regardless of focus behavior.

## Test plan

- [x] Added test case verifying error is thrown when shadowRoot is missing
- [x] All existing SlotMixin tests pass
- [x] OverlayController test passes reliably on Firefox (verified with multiple local runs)
- [x] All browser tests pass (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)

Closes #1902

author: jpgrayson
body:
zsh dynamic completions would add a trailing space after all completions, including directories. This prevented natural path completion. Users had to delete the trailing space before continuing to type or tab-complete within the directory.

The fix is for the dynamic completion script to separate completions into directories and non-directories, and providing the directory completions to zsh with a different _describe invocation.

For directories:
1. Strip the trailing slash from the completion value
2. Let zsh add it back as a suffix using `_describe -S '/'`
3. Also provide `-r '/'` to make the slash auto-removable when typing '/'

This makes dynamic path completions reasonably emulate zsh-native file completions.

This matches the behavior already implemented for bash completions which uses 'compopt -o nospace' to achieve the same result.

Fixes: #6178
Ref: https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/issues/5582

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a deterministic, machine-readable installation flow for core attention packages on `cu130` nightly builds. 
- Ensure reliable install attempts and import validation for `flash-attn`, `sageattention`, `sageattention2`, and `triton-windows` with clear gating for failures. 
- Move fragile/performance wheel installs out of the generic `stage1.sh` flow so the workflow can manage ordering and fallbacks. 
- Surface install results to CI logs and artifacts to avoid silent failures.

### Description
- Add `builder-cu130/scripts/install_core_attention.ps1` which attempts installation in order (PyPI binary, AI-windows-whl fallback, source build if allowed), runs import checks, and writes a JSON manifest to `accel_manifest.json` containing `{name, version, source, success, error_if_any}`. 
- Update `builder-cu130/stage1.sh` to skip core attention installs when the environment variable `SKIP_CORE_ATTENTION=1` is set. 
- Wire the cu130 nightly workflow (`.github/workflows/build-cu130-nightly.yml`) to set `SKIP_CORE_ATTENTION`, run the new `install_core_attention.ps1` step, print a short table summary to the logs, and upload `builder-cu130/accel_manifest.json` as an artifact. 
- Preserve the existing `attempt_install_xformers.ps1` and downstream build/packaging stages.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change; the new installer and workflow steps are exercised by the nightly GitHub Actions job. 
- Changes were committed after local edits and basic syntax checks for the added PowerShell and bash changes. 
- The intended CI validation is that the nightly workflow produces `accel_manifest.json` and the manifest is uploaded as an artifact, with import checks reflected in the manifest. 
- The installer gates failing optional packages (keeps workflow green) and throws only if a package marked `Required` fails to install.

body: # Objective - After a series of optimizations making render and postupdate more parallel, `write_batched_instance_buffers` was regularly one of the largest spans with very low thread use, sitting at 4ms in 1 4ms frame. This makes it an ideal target to improve throughput. Note this screenshot doesn't include some visibility system optimizations: ## Solution - Spawn tasks for writing buffers to the GPU. This is especially helpful for `current_input_buffer` and `previous_input_buffer`, which take about the same time and are the longest buffer writes - moving these to tasks effectively halves the time spent in the system. - In the 250k bevymark_3d stress test, this saves 1.7ms in the system, and 2.8ms in frame time frametime system ## Testing - `cargo rer bevymark_3d --features=debug,trace_tracy -- --benchmark --waves 250 --per-wave 1000`

body:
## ✅ 方針

1. **管理画面のREST（/admin/contents/:id）は数値IDで運用する**（Issue3の意図を維持）
2. そのために **`Content#to_param` を “必ず id” に固定する**
3. その上で **`form_with` から `url:` を撤去**して Rails 標準に戻す

FriendlyId は「slug生成」用途として残してOK（URLに使わないだけ）。

---

# 1) `Content#to_param` を追加（重要）

`app/models/content.rb` に追加してください（既存の class 内どこでもOK）：

```ruby
def to_param
  id.to_s
end
```

これで **FriendlyId がいても管理画面のパスは常に数値ID** になります。

> `id-slug` 形式は今回おすすめしません。
> `Content.find("1-about")` が **DB側で bigint キャストに失敗して落ちる**可能性があるためです（Railsが勝手に `to_i` してくれる保証が薄い）。

---

# 2) 管理画面フォームから `url:` を撤去

`app/views/admin/contents/_form.html.erb`

今：

```erb
<% form_url = content.persisted? ? admin_content_path(content.id) : admin_contents_path %>
<%= form_with model: [:admin, content],
              url: form_url,
              local: true,
              html: { multipart: true } do |f| %>
```

↓ これに変更：

```erb
<%= form_with model: [:admin, content], local: true do |f| %>
```

* `multipart: true` は file_field があれば自動で付きます（消してOK）

Closes #79 
Relates to #10

author: copilot
body:
Stateless, zero-database resume analysis tool that compares resumes against job descriptions with explainable, ATS-aware scoring.

## Architecture

- **Parser** (`app/parser/`) - PDF, DOCX, TXT extraction with section detection
- **Analyzer** (`app/analyzer/`) - Job description parsing, skill classification (required/preferred), seniority detection
- **Scorer** (`app/scorer/`) - Multi-dimensional scoring: skill match (40%), experience (25%), keywords (20%), ATS (15%)
- **Report** (`app/report/`) - Markdown, JSON, PDF output generation
- **Knowledge Base** - 100+ skill synonyms, semantic groupings, normalization (JS → JavaScript)

## Interfaces

- CLI: `python -m app.main analyze resume.pdf job.txt`
- API: FastAPI at `/analyze`, `/parse/resume`, `/parse/job`

## Privacy Guarantees

All processing in-memory. No database, no storage, no accounts, no analytics.

## Usage

```python
from app.parser.resume_parser import parse_resume_text
from app.analyzer.job_analyzer import analyze_job_description
from app.scorer.match_scorer import calculate_match

resume = parse_resume_text(resume_text)
job = analyze_job_description(job_text)
result = calculate_match(resume, job)

print(f"Score: {result.overall_score}/100 ({result.overall_grade})")
print(f"Missing: {[s.normalized_name for s in result.missing_required_skills]}")
```

## Testing

65 unit tests covering parser, analyzer, scorer, and report modules.

author: sourodip-1
body:
# Bug Fix Report: `savedPalettes` Undefined Error

## Problem Description

The application crashed with the following error:

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')
```

This occurred in `App.jsx` when trying to render the list of saved palettes.

## Root Cause Analysis

The error originated in the `fetchSavedPalettes` function:

```javascript
// Problemetic Code
const response = await fetch("/api/palettes").then((res) => res.json());
setSavedPalettes(response.data); // <--- Error Source
```

The backend API `/api/palettes` returns a direct array (e.g., `[...]`), but the frontend code expected an object with a `data` property (e.g., `{ data: [...] }`).

- `response` was `[...]` (Array)
- `response.data` was `undefined`
- `setSavedPalettes(undefined)` caused state to be `undefined`
- `savedPalettes.length` threw the error.

## Fix Implementation

### 1. Robust Data Fetching

Updated `fetchSavedPalettes` in `App.jsx` to handle both direct array responses and object-wrapped responses.

```javascript
// Fixed Code
const response = await fetch("/api/palettes").then((res) => res.json());
setSavedPalettes(Array.isArray(response) ? response : response.data || []);
```

### 2. Defensive Rendering

Added optional chaining (`?.`) to the rendering logic to prevent crashes even if the state is null/undefined.

```javascript
// Fixed Code
{savedPalettes?.length > 0 && (
  // ...
)}
```

## Status

The application now correctly loads the palettes from the server without crashing.

body:
Problem:
- CI tests were failing due to explicit `executablePath: undefined`
  being passed to Playwright's launchOptions in CI environment
- This prevented Playwright from using its default browser installation

Changes:
1. Only set launchOptions with custom executablePath in local dev environment
2. In CI environment, omit launchOptions entirely to use Playwright's defaults
3. Set reuseExistingServer to true in local dev to avoid port conflicts
   (false in CI for clean test runs)

This should resolve the E2E test failures in GitHub Actions.

author: robzolkos
body:
## Summary

- Fix CLI to nest request parameters under resource-specific keys as expected by the Rails API
- Add input/output validation to e2e tests to verify data is actually persisted

## Problem

The CLI was sending request parameters at the top level:
```json
{ "board_id": "...", "title": "...", "description": "..." }
```

But the Rails API expects them nested under a resource key:
```json
{ "board_id": "...", "card": { "title": "...", "description": "..." } }
```

This caused data to silently not be saved because Rails' `params.expect(card: [...])` couldn't find the nested parameters.

## Changes

### Fixed parameter nesting in:
- `card.go`: nest under `card: {...}`
- `board.go`: nest under `board: {...}`
- `column.go`: nest under `column: {...}`
- `step.go`: nest under `step: {...}`

### Enhanced e2e tests to verify input == output:
- **Board**: verify name after create
- **Card**: verify title, description (plain text + HTML)
- **Column**: verify name and color after create
- **Comment**: verify body (plain text + HTML) on create and update

## Why e2e tests didn't catch this before
- E2E tests skip when `FIZZY_TEST_TOKEN` is not set
- CI doesn't have API credentials configured
- Unit tests mock the HTTP layer and were written with the same incorrect understanding

## Test plan
- [x] All unit tests pass
- [x] All e2e CRUD tests pass with real API credentials
- [x] Verified input/output validation catches data not being saved

body:
## Summary

Add mainnet deployment support for IGRA Orchestra with configurable network settings.

### Key Changes

- **Network flag fix**: Mainnet is the default (no `--mainnet` flag exists)
- **DNS seeding**: Enabled for mainnet (automatic peer discovery), disabled for testnet/devnet
- **IGRA_ENABLE toggle**: Disable IGRA adapter during initial kaspad sync for faster sync
- **Port configuration**: All ports now configurable via environment variables
- **Kaspad isolation**: Removed external access (traefik routing removed, internal docker network only)

### Port Configuration

| Network | gRPC | P2P | Borsh | JSON |
|---------|------|-----|-------|------|
| Mainnet | 16110 | 16111 | 17110 | 18110 |
| Testnet | 16210 | 16211 | 17210 | 18210 |

### Files Changed

- `docker-compose.yml` - Network flag conditional, removed kaspad expose/ports/traefik
- `.env.mainnet.example` - New mainnet configuration template
- `.env.example`, `.env.backend.example`, `.env.backend-with-rpc.example` - Added port variables
- `doc/quick-setup-mainnet.md` - New mainnet deployment guide
- `doc/kaspa-wallet.md` - Updated with mainnet instructions

## Test plan

- [x] Verify `docker compose config` parses correctly
- [x] Test kaspad startup with `NETWORK=mainnet` and `IGRA_ENABLE=false`
- [x] Test kaspad startup with `NETWORK=mainnet` and `IGRA_ENABLE=true`
- [x] Test kaspad startup with `NETWORK=testnet` (backward compatibility)
- [x] Verify kaspad uses DNS seeding on mainnet (automatic peer discovery)

This change adds support for viewing and caching release notes, migrates release caching from files to an SQLite database, and displays the notes in a dialog on the frontend with dynamic action buttons.

---

---
## Summary by cubic
Adds release notes to the Play page and moves release caching from files to SQLite. Notes are fetched on demand from GitHub, cached in the DB, and shown in a dialog with a dynamic action button.

- **New Features**
  - Release Notes button in the selector opens a dialog; confirm text adapts to selection (Upgrade/Downgrade/Pre-Installed/Install).
  - New fetch_release_notes command checks DB first, then fetches GitHub release by tag and caches notes.
  - SQLite now stores release_notes; GitHubRelease includes body; frontend adds fetchReleaseNotes and a releaseNotes query key.

- **Migration**
  - releases table gains release_notes (auto ALTER TABLE on startup).
  - DB seeds releases and assets from resources/releases/*.json; file-based cache is no longer used.
  - No manual steps required.

<sup>Written for commit a48c476947f752aded82aa2401ded2e02c407c98. Summary will update on new commits.</sup>
